questions.question:

Hearing those words / from his mouth, was / hard than I thought.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**hard than I thought**."

• The correct phrase is "harder than I thought," with the comparative form of the adjective "hard."
 
• The error is that "hard" is used as an adverb instead of the comparative form "harder."
 
• The correct sentence would be:
 
 
• "Hearing those words from his mouth was harder than I thought."
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.

• **Example:** He was astonished to find out that he had won the lottery.
 
 
 
• Hence, the more appropriate word to replace "amazed" in this context is **"astonished"**.

• **Example:** His calculations were accurate and reliable.
 
 
 
• **Swamped** (व्यस्त): Overwhelmed with too much work or tasks.
 
 
• **Example:** The team was swamped with deadlines and assignments.
